facts.title: The Greatest
facts.statement: Muhammad Ali won the world heavyweight title three times, refused the Vietnam draft, and was stripped of his title for over three years at his peak.
facts.question: Which boxer called himself 'The Greatest' and won the heavyweight title three times?

facts.title: Three World Cups
facts.statement: Pelé is the only player to win three FIFA World Cups, in 1958, 1962 and 1970, the first at just seventeen.
facts.question: Who is the only footballer to have won three World Cups?

facts.title: Six rings in Chicago
facts.statement: Michael Jordan won six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls and was named Finals MVP all six times.
facts.question: Which basketball player won six NBA titles with the Chicago Bulls?

facts.title: The fastest man
facts.statement: Usain Bolt holds the 100 m world record at 9.58 seconds, set in Berlin in 2009, and won eight Olympic golds.
facts.question: Who holds the men's 100 metres world record of 9.58 seconds?

facts.title: 23 Grand Slam singles titles
facts.statement: Serena Williams won 23 Grand Slam singles titles in the Open Era, including the 2017 Australian Open while pregnant.
facts.question: Which tennis player won 23 Grand Slam singles titles in the Open Era?

facts.title: The most decorated Olympian
facts.statement: Michael Phelps won 28 Olympic medals, 23 of them gold — more than any other athlete in history.
facts.question: Which swimmer is the most decorated Olympian of all time?

facts.title: The Hand of God
facts.statement: Diego Maradona scored twice against England in the 1986 World Cup quarter-final: once illegally with his hand, and minutes later with a run past five defenders.
facts.question: Which footballer scored the 'Hand of God' goal in 1986?
facts.hook: The same four minutes produced the most notorious and the most admired goal in World Cup history.

facts.title: Eight Wimbledon titles
facts.statement: Roger Federer won a record eight Wimbledon men's singles titles and 20 Grand Slams in total.
facts.question: Which player has won the most Wimbledon men's singles titles?

facts.title: The gymnast with her own moves
facts.statement: Simone Biles has five skills named after her in the Code of Points, more than any other gymnast.
facts.question: Which gymnast has five different skills named after her?

facts.title: Four golds in Berlin
facts.statement: Jesse Owens won four gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics, undermining Nazi propaganda about racial superiority in front of Hitler.
facts.question: Which athlete won four golds at the 1936 Berlin Olympics?

facts.title: The perfect 10
facts.statement: Nadia Comăneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics in 1976 — the scoreboard could only display three digits, so it read 1.00.
facts.question: Which gymnast scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic history?
facts.hook: The scoreboard literally could not show the score.

facts.title: The Great One
facts.statement: Wayne Gretzky holds more NHL records than any player; his assists alone would make him the league's all-time leading scorer.
facts.question: Which ice hockey player is nicknamed 'The Great One'?

facts.title: The Ballon d'Or record
facts.statement: Lionel Messi has won a record eight Ballon d'Or awards and captained Argentina to the 2022 World Cup.
facts.question: Which footballer has won the most Ballon d'Or awards?

facts.title: The Sultan of Swat
facts.statement: Babe Ruth transformed baseball into a power-hitting game and hit 714 home runs, a record that stood for 39 years.
facts.question: Which baseball player was known as the Sultan of Swat?

facts.title: Kings of Europe
facts.statement: Real Madrid have won the European Cup and Champions League more times than any other club, by a wide margin.
facts.question: Which club has won the most European Cup / Champions League titles?

facts.title: 27 World Series
facts.statement: The New York Yankees have won 27 World Series titles, more than any other Major League Baseball franchise.
facts.question: Which team has won the most World Series titles?

facts.title: The men in black
facts.statement: The All Blacks, New Zealand's rugby union team, have the highest win rate of any international team in any major sport, and perform the haka before matches.
facts.question: What is New Zealand's national rugby union team called?
facts.wikiTitle: New Zealand national rugby union team

facts.title: The oldest team in Formula One
facts.statement: Scuderia Ferrari is the oldest and most successful team in Formula One, and the only one to have competed in every season since 1950.
facts.question: Which is the oldest and most successful team in Formula One?

facts.title: The Celtics dynasty
facts.statement: The Boston Celtics won eight consecutive NBA championships from 1959 to 1966, a run unmatched in major American sport.
facts.question: Which NBA team won eight straight championships from 1959 to 1966?

facts.title: The Red Devils
facts.statement: Manchester United have won a record 20 English top-flight league titles.
facts.question: Which club has won the most English top-flight league titles?

facts.title: Most World Cup wins
facts.statement: Brazil have won the FIFA World Cup five times and are the only nation to have played in every tournament.
facts.question: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cups?

facts.title: The 2022 World Cup
facts.statement: Argentina won the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, beating France on penalties after a 3–3 draw widely called the greatest final ever played.
facts.question: Which country won the 2022 FIFA World Cup?

facts.title: The first World Cup
facts.statement: Uruguay hosted and won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930, and won again in 1950.
facts.question: Which country hosted and won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?

facts.title: The home of cricket
facts.statement: Cricket originated in England, where the Marylebone Cricket Club has maintained the laws of the game since 1787.
facts.question: In which country did cricket originate?

facts.title: The national sport of Japan
facts.statement: Sumo is Japan's national sport, with rituals drawn from Shinto and a professional history stretching back centuries.
facts.question: Which country is the home of sumo wrestling?

facts.title: The birthplace of the Olympics
facts.statement: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia in Greece from 776 BC, and the first modern Games returned to Athens in 1896.
facts.question: In which country did the Olympic Games originate?

facts.title: The Tour de France
facts.statement: The Tour de France, first held in 1903, covers around 3,500 km over three weeks and finishes in Paris.
facts.question: In which country is the Tour de France principally held?

facts.title: The 2024 Summer Olympics
facts.statement: Paris hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics, becoming only the second city to host three times.
facts.question: Which city hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics?

facts.title: The delayed Olympics
facts.statement: Tokyo hosted the 2020 Summer Olympics in 2021, postponed by the COVID-19 pandemic and held almost without spectators.
facts.question: Which city hosted the Summer Olympics that were postponed to 2021?

facts.title: The first South American Olympics
facts.statement: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics, the first held in South America.
facts.question: Which city hosted the first Olympic Games in South America?

facts.title: The 2012 Games
facts.statement: London hosted the 2012 Summer Olympics, becoming the first city to host the modern Games three times.
facts.question: Which city became the first to host the Summer Olympics three times?

facts.title: The first modern Games
facts.statement: Athens hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896, with 14 nations competing.
facts.question: Which city hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896?

facts.title: The Bird's Nest
facts.statement: Beijing hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and in 2022 became the first city to host both a Summer and a Winter Games.
facts.question: Which city hosted both the 2008 Summer and 2022 Winter Olympics?

facts.title: Players in a football team
facts.statement: An association football team fields 11 players, including the goalkeeper.
facts.question: How many players from each team are on the pitch in association football?

facts.title: Players in a basketball team
facts.statement: A basketball team has five players on court at a time.
facts.question: How many players from each team are on court in basketball?

facts.title: Players in rugby union
facts.statement: A rugby union team fields 15 players; rugby league fields 13.
facts.question: How many players are in a rugby union team on the field?

facts.title: Players on the ice
facts.statement: An ice hockey team has six players on the ice, including the goaltender.
facts.question: How many players from each team are on the ice in hockey?

facts.title: Players in a baseball team
facts.statement: A baseball team fields nine players, and the batting order runs to nine as well.
facts.question: How many players from a team are on the field in baseball?

facts.title: Players in water polo
facts.statement: A water polo team has seven players in the pool, including the goalkeeper.
facts.question: How many players from each team are in the pool in water polo?

facts.title: Three goals
facts.statement: A hat-trick is three goals by one player in a single match. The term comes from cricket, where a bowler taking three wickets in three balls won a hat.
facts.question: What is it called when one player scores three goals in a match?
facts.hook: It started in cricket, and the prize was an actual hat.

facts.title: Zero in tennis
facts.statement: In tennis, a score of zero is called love, probably from the French l'oeuf — 'the egg' — for its shape.
facts.question: What is the term for a score of zero in tennis?

facts.title: One under par
facts.statement: In golf, a birdie is one stroke under par for a hole; an eagle is two under and an albatross three under.
facts.question: In golf, what is a score of one stroke under par called?

facts.title: The end of a chess game
facts.statement: Checkmate ends a chess game: the king is under attack and no legal move can save it. The word comes from Persian shah mat, 'the king is helpless'.
facts.question: What is the winning position in chess called?

facts.title: The offside rule
facts.statement: Offside in football penalises an attacker who is nearer the goal line than both the ball and the second-last defender when the ball is played to them.
facts.question: Which football rule penalises an attacker for being ahead of the second-last defender?

facts.title: The marathon distance
facts.statement: A marathon is 42.195 km. The odd distance was fixed at the 1908 London Olympics so the race could finish in front of the royal box.
facts.question: How long is a marathon?
facts.hook: The extra 195 metres exist so royalty would not have to move.

facts.title: The sport of the slam dunk
facts.statement: Basketball was invented in 1891 by James Naismith, who nailed peach baskets to a gymnasium balcony.
facts.question: In which sport would you perform a slam dunk?

facts.title: The sport of the birdie
facts.statement: Golf is played over 18 holes, a number standardised by the Old Course at St Andrews in Scotland.
facts.question: In which sport do players aim for birdies and eagles?

facts.title: The sport of the ace
facts.statement: Tennis is played on grass, clay and hard courts, and its four Grand Slams each use a different surface combination.
facts.question: In which sport is an unreturnable serve called an ace?

facts.title: The sport of the wicket
facts.statement: Cricket's longest format, Test cricket, can last five days and still end in a draw.
facts.question: In which sport does a bowler try to take a wicket?

facts.title: The sport of the foil
facts.statement: Fencing has three weapons — foil, épée and sabre — each with its own target area and rules.
facts.question: In which sport do competitors use a foil, épée or sabre?

facts.title: The gentle way
facts.statement: Judo, founded by Jigoro Kano in 1882, means 'the gentle way' and uses an opponent's force against them.
facts.question: Which martial art's name means 'the gentle way'?

facts.title: The oldest board game still played
facts.statement: Go originated in China over 2,500 years ago and has more possible board positions than there are atoms in the observable universe.
facts.question: Which ancient Chinese board game uses black and white stones on a 19x19 grid?
facts.hook: More legal positions than atoms in the universe, on a board of 361 points.

facts.title: The royal game
facts.statement: Chess in its modern form emerged in Europe in the 15th century, developing from the Indian game chaturanga.
facts.question: Which board game features a king, queen, bishops, knights and rooks?

facts.title: Buying property
facts.statement: Monopoly was derived from The Landlord's Game, designed to demonstrate the harm of land monopolies — the opposite of how it is played today.
facts.question: Which board game involves buying properties and collecting rent?
facts.hook: It was invented to criticise landlords, then sold as a game about becoming one.

facts.title: Words for points
facts.statement: Scrabble assigns letter values by frequency in English; Q and Z are worth 10 points each because they are rare.
facts.question: Which board game scores players for forming words on a grid?

facts.title: Dice and doubling
facts.statement: Backgammon is one of the oldest known board games, roughly 5,000 years old, combining dice luck with positional strategy.
facts.question: Which ancient game uses dice, checkers and a doubling cube?

facts.title: The solved game
facts.statement: Checkers, or draughts, was weakly solved by computers in 2007: perfect play by both sides always ends in a draw.
facts.question: Which board game was proved in 2007 to end in a draw with perfect play?

facts.title: The home of tennis
facts.statement: Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world, founded in 1877, and the only Grand Slam still played on grass.
facts.question: Which is the oldest tennis tournament in the world?

facts.title: The green jacket
facts.statement: Augusta National in Georgia hosts the Masters every April, and the winner receives a green jacket.
facts.question: Which golf course hosts the Masters Tournament?

facts.title: The largest stadium in Europe
facts.statement: Camp Nou in Barcelona is the largest football stadium in Europe by capacity.
facts.question: Which Barcelona stadium is the largest football ground in Europe?

facts.title: The Theatre of Dreams
facts.statement: Old Trafford, Manchester United's ground since 1910, is nicknamed the Theatre of Dreams.
facts.question: Which stadium is known as the Theatre of Dreams?

facts.title: The world's most famous arena
facts.statement: Madison Square Garden in New York hosts the Knicks and Rangers and calls itself the world's most famous arena.
facts.question: Which New York arena is home to the Knicks and the Rangers?

facts.title: The Olympic rings
facts.statement: The five Olympic rings represent the five inhabited continents, and their colours were chosen so that every national flag then in use contained at least one of them.
facts.question: What do the five Olympic rings represent?

facts.title: The Ashes
facts.statement: The Ashes is contested between England and Australia in cricket, named after a mock obituary declaring English cricket dead in 1882.
facts.question: Which two countries contest cricket's Ashes series?

facts.title: The Grand Slam of tennis
facts.statement: Tennis has four Grand Slam tournaments: the Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open.
facts.question: How many Grand Slam tournaments are there in tennis?

facts.title: The yellow jersey
facts.statement: The maillot jaune, or yellow jersey, is worn by the overall leader of the Tour de France, coloured to match the newspaper that founded the race.
facts.question: What colour jersey does the overall leader of the Tour de France wear?
facts.hook: Yellow because the sponsoring newspaper was printed on yellow paper.

facts.title: The World Cup interval
facts.statement: The FIFA World Cup is held every four years, and has been since 1930 apart from a break for the Second World War.
facts.question: How often is the FIFA World Cup held?

facts.title: The sport played at the Superbowl
facts.statement: The Super Bowl is the championship game of the National Football League, played in American football and typically the most watched US broadcast of the year.
facts.question: Which sport's championship game is the Super Bowl?

facts.title: The Formula One points leader
facts.statement: Formula One awards its drivers' championship on points across a season, with Michael Schumacher and Lewis Hamilton tied on a record seven titles each.
facts.question: Which two drivers share the record of seven Formula One world titles?
facts.wikiTitle: List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions

facts.title: The sport of the peloton
facts.statement: In road cycling, the peloton is the main bunch of riders, whose drafting saves each rider up to 40% of their energy.
facts.question: In which sport does the main group of competitors form a peloton?
